comments.body: Note on the red macOS builds: they fail in the faiss/OpenMP build step on the macOS runner, which also hit another PR on 10-28. This PR only changes `chat.py` and adds `tests/test_anthropic_default_model.py`. Happy to merge `main` in to re-run if that helps.

Verified the bug and the test. Reverting the one-line change makes the new test fail:

```
E   AssertionError: assert 'claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022' == 'claude-haiku-4-5'
```

So the report is accurate: `get_llm({"type": "anthropic"})` with no model was building a model Anthropic has retired.

**On the red macOS jobs — they are not a faiss/OpenMP build failure, and they are not pre-existing.** `main` is currently 75/75 green. This branch was 3 commits behind, and one of those commits is the fix:

```
85fc9893  test: skip native HNSW append on macOS
```

It widens a skip from `darwin and platform.machine() == "x86_64"` to plain `darwin`, because the native `index.add()` call aborts inside the FAISS bindings and takes the pytest session with it. This branch still had the Intel-only condition, so the ARM runners ran the test and died — which is why `macos-15-intel` passed while every ARM runner failed. (ARM Python 3.10 passing is the one thing that does not fit that explanation; I did not chase it down.)

**I pushed two things:** a merge of `main`, and one follow-up change.

The follow-up: rather than syncing the two copies of the default, I removed the duplication. The factory now passes `model` only when the config sets one, so `AnthropicChat`'s signature default is the single place the default is written:

```python
anthropic_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
    "api_key": llm_config.get("api_key"),
    "base_url": llm_config.get("base_url"),
}
if model:
    anthropic_kwargs["model"] = model
return AnthropicChat(**anthropic_kwargs)
```

The bug existed *because* the string was written twice; syncing them leaves the drift free to recur, and `CLAUDE.md` asks for one implementation per feature. Your tests still earn their place after the change — I re-introduced a divergent literal in the new structure and they still failed, so they guard the regression rather than becoming tautological.

CI's exact lint command and `ty check` both pass.

Worth noting for later: the other seven providers in `get_llm` have the same duplication. They are all in sync today, so nothing is broken — Anthropic is just where the drift happened to fire.
